newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy named Chicago Housing winner.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy named Chicago Housing winner.

text.p: Wisconsin Energy Corp said Friday its Wisconsin Electric Power Co unit was named the winning bidder to supply power to Chicago Housing Authority.
But the housing authority's current supplier is arguing that the authority cannot legally enter the deal.
The housing authority currently purchases about 140 million kilowatts of power annually from Commonwealth Edison Co, a unit of Unicom Corp, a Wisconsin Energy spokeswoman said.
The housing authority hopes to save $4 million to $5 million on its approximately $10 million energy costs under the Wisconsin Electric deal, the spokeswoman said.
Wisconsin Electric will buy the power and transmit it to the housing authority using Commonwealth Edison equipment under the deal, the spokeswoman said.

Commonwealth Edison said in a statement that the housing authority does not qualify as a wholesale consumer under current federal and state law and therefore cannot enter an agreement to purchase power from Wisonsin Electric.
"Only legitimate wholesale customers, such as municipal utility companies, can contract directly for wholesale electricity purchases," Commonwealth Edison said in the statement.

The Wisconsin Electric spokeswoman said the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission must decide whether the housing authority qualifies as a wholesale customer before Wisconsin Electric can begin providing power.
